newsitem.title: USA: US magnesium mulls Hydro's dumping query.
newsitem.headline: US magnesium mulls Hydro's dumping query.

text.p: The U.S. magnesium industry was taking its time to mull a suggestion from Norway's Hydro Magnesium that it dumped metal on the European market.

Earlier on Wednesday Hydro Magnesium's vice-president of marketing, Robert Edgar, said U.S. producers were selling metal in Europe at prices well below what they sold at in their home market - one of the criteria for dumping.
In the past, U.S. producers successfully filed an anti-dumping suit against imports of pure magnesium from Hydro's Canadian operation.
Magnesium is used in aluminum and steel production, and for making auto components.
Howard Kaplan, marketing and sales vice president of Utah-based Magnesium Corp declined to comment on Hydro's claims.
Washington-based Northwest Alloys, wholly-owned by Alcoa, said it was not selling any magnesium in Europe, or shipping to Alcoa's plants there for use in aluminum production.
Officials at Dow Magnesium in Texas, part of Dow Chemical, were not available for comment.
But some traders doubted whether U.S. producers would be selling much metal in Europe, given the inland and international freight charges, financing and 5.3 percent duty they face.

"It just does not make sense to me, especially when European consumers can buy Chinese at cheaper prices or duty paid Russian and Ukrainian. We have not come into competition with U.S. producers in Europe," the trader said.
MagCorp's Kaplan said the company always "maintained a position in all the major magnesium markets of the world" which would include Europe.
U.S. pure magnesium spot market prices are in the $1.41 to $1.44 per pound range, compared to Hydro's new European price of DM5.40 per kilo or $1.54.
Dow Magnesium, part of Dow Chemical, and MagCorp recently cut their U.S. pure magnesium prices to $1.80 per pound. Northwest does not post a price as Alcoa consumes most of its output.
Magnesium industry officials noted that Hydro Magnesium was accusing U.S. producers of dumping even though it has just posted a lower list price in Europe than in the U.S.
"He (Edgar) is the price leader and he has set a lower price in Europe for a long time," the officials said.
Hydro brought its U.S. list price down to $1.80 per pound on Wednesday to fall in line with domestic producers.
Meanwhile the U.S. magnesium market was said to be steady with prices off the lows and even edging up slightly in some cases.

Kaplan said much would depend on a bounce back in aluminum and figures from the International Magnesium Association showed that Western world producer inventory fell to 33,000 tonnes in November from 38,000 tonnes in September.
However, the holiday period in December would probably have a temporary dampening effect on demand as well, Kaplan added.
